title: Capacity runway & surge-readiness Q3 initiative — playbook, experiments, and rollout
text:
Capacity runway & surge-readiness Q3 initiative — playbook, experiments, and rollout

description:
Goal: produce a deployable Q3 playbook that reduces tail latency during sudden demand surges for dedicated pools while minimizing committed spend. This ticket coordinates PM engineering and SRE work to define metrics, run controlled surge experiments, and ship automated rollback/fastpath policies. Deliverables: 1) playbook doc with signal contracts and escalations; 2) 3 surge experiments (small/medium/large) with success criteria; 3) a canary rollout plan for conservative fastpath expansion; 4) dashboard and alert surface to validate in prod-like traffic.

acceptance_criteria:
Playbook doc published in Confluence with runbook steps, owner matrix, and decision tree
Three surge experiments run in staging with collected telemetry and postmortem notes
Automated fastpath expansion policy merged behind feature flag and tested in canary
Dashboard tile showing capacity runway, prewarm utilization, and surge gap metric; runbook alerts linked to PagerDuty escalation
Cost impact model updated with per-surge delta and included in release notes

updates:
2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and billing — agreed on three experiment contours and primary metric (surge_gap_pct)
2026-03-02: SRE proposed signal contract draft (queue-depth, request-latency delta, prewarm-occupancy) — PM requested explicit failure modes
2026-03-05: Runtime team scoped feature flag for fastpath expansion; initial API surface for tiered expansion submitted as RFC (#RFC-5467)
2026-03-10: Design/Console team will add a compact dashboard tile in the capacity overview to visualize runway and surge gap — design handoff scheduled
